newsitem.title: USA: Disney close to buying Starwave stake - source.
newsitem.headline: Disney close to buying Starwave stake - source.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. is in talks to buy a major stake in Starwave Corp., the Web site company owned by Microsoft Corp. co-founder Paul Allen, a source familiar with the negotiations said Friday.
Disney and Starwave officials declined to comment.
The source said Disney was close to a deal that would give it a major stake, possibly a controlling stake, in the company, which operates popular sports and entertainment sites on the Internet.

The Los Angeles Times reported Friday that Disney had agreed to buy a one-third interest and take management control of Starwave in a deal that would value the Bellevue, Wash.-based company at about $300 million.
C/Net, an Internet news site in which Allen owns a major stake, said a Disney-Starwave deal could conclude within two weeks.

"The stories that you've seen are speculative, and we always decline to comment on speculation," said Susan Pierson, a spokesman for the billionaire investor who has assembled a portfolio of technology and entertainment companies.
The source familiar with the talks, who declined to be identified, said premature publication of the news could hamper the negotiations.
Disney and Starwave already operate ESPNet-SportsZone, a joint venture that is considered one of the most commercially successful sites on the Internet. ESPN is a unit of Disney.
The joint venture also operates official Web sites for the National Football League, National Basketball Association and NASCAR auto racing.

In addition, Starwave executives have been negotiating with Disney's ABC News to launch an Internet news site that would compete with MSNBC, a joint venture launched last year by Microsoft and General Electric Co.'s NBC network.
Founded in 1993, Starwave has about 300 employees and also operates the Mr. Showbiz and Family Planet Web sites as well as Outside Online in partnership with Outside magazine.
